chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from al-Ala' from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the vessels of the People of the Covenant and the Magians, so he said: 'Do not eat in their vessels, nor from their food that they cook, nor in their vessels from which they drink wine.'

key_terms.أهل الذمة: People of the Covenant (non-Muslims living under Muslim rule)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating from the vessels of non-Muslims in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) delineates the boundaries of ritual purity by prohibiting the consumption of food cooked by Ahl al-Dhimmah and Magians, as well as eating from their specific vessels, a ruling that underscores the Shia emphasis on the potential impurity of their culinary practices. This hadith specifically highlights the exclusion of vessels used for wine, linking dietary laws to the broader concept of *najāsah* (impurity) associated with non-Muslims in Shia jurisprudence. The ruling reflects the scholarly tradition of distinguishing between the people themselves and their material possessions, particularly regarding items used for consuming intoxicants.
